The Judiciary of Uganda reports that its Electronic Court Case Management Information System (ECCMIS) is implemented, with progress in automating lower courts and a tailored version in the Anti-Corruption Division.
The Judiciary of Uganda says ECCMIS went live on 1 March 2022 in seven courts, automating and tracking a court case's life cycle and replacing the former CCAS.

The Judiciary of Uganda says its Electronic Court Case Management Information System (ECCMIS) had expanded to 31 court stations across five rollout clusters by July 2025, after going live on 1 March 2022.
The Judiciary's FY2024/25 performance report says ECCMIS was rolled out to 23 courts that year and is operational in 11.5 percent of courts.
The Judiciary says ECCMIS gave litigants 24-hour access to e-filing and that cases are filed and fees paid online, per the Permanent Secretary to the Judiciary.
The Judiciary describes a litigant at Jinja High Court checking updates on her case file on her phone through ECCMIS.
The Judiciary's project manager Joseph Ssinabulya says the Electronic Court Case Management Information System (ECCMIS) has already been introduced in more than 56 courts.

Kalisho Info reports that Uganda's Judiciary rolled out the Electronic Court Case Management Information System (ECCMIS) across the Cluster Eight courts of the Mbarara High Court Circuit on 18 May 2026, after a national launch in 2022 and earlier clusters.
Kalisho Info reports that ECCMIS lets litigants and lawyers file documents electronically through a public portal.
Kalisho Info reports that ECCMIS gives real-time case status updates and the public portal gives access to case information across all jurisdictions.

The Observer reports that the judiciary's Electronic Court Case Management Information System (ECCMIS) is in use, with courts operating largely on digital systems and a 1 July 2026 paperless deadline set by the Chief Justice's circular.
The Observer reports that through ECCMIS lawyers and litigants can file cases and pleadings, submit documents and request hearing dates online, per the High Court deputy registrar.
The Observer reports that ULII hosts more than 41,000 decisions from the High Court, Court of Appeal, Supreme Court and tribunals, searchable online, with 350,000 users a month.
